docs.title: cheersafe
docs.text:
CHEERSafe: Hurricane loss analysis package for building properties, hazard data, and loss models.

This package provides comprehensive tools for hurricane damage and loss assessment, including building inventory management, load calculations, damage probability analysis, damage ratio calculations, and loss estimation.

A configuration management class for the CHEERSafe package.

This class provides global configuration settings for the CHEERSafe hurricane damage and loss assessment model. It manages execution behavior, data loading preferences, file paths, and processing parameters used throughout the package.

Attributes:

Name Type Description AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS bool

Flag to control automatic execution of methods. When True, methods are executed automatically during object initialization. Default is True.

AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS bool

Flag to control automatic loading of datasets. When True, datasets are loaded automatically during object initialization. Default is True.

INPUTS_PATH str

The directory path where input data files are stored. Default is 'Inputs'.

OUTPUTS_PATH str

The directory path where output files will be saved. Default is 'Outputs'.

NUM_OF_ITERATIONS int

The number of iterations to perform in Monte Carlo simulations and other iterative processes. Default is 3000.

NUM_OF_WORKERS int

The number of parallel workers to use for multi-threaded operations. Default is 4.

NUM_OF_WORKERS_SAMPLING int

The number of parallel workers to use specifically for sampling operations. Default is 1.

RANDOM_SEED int

The default random seed used for reproducible stochastic calculations. Default is 42.

EXPORT_DETAILED_DAMAGE_RATIOS bool

Flag to enable export of detailed damage ratio breakdowns to CSV files. When True, detailed component-level damage ratios are collected during Monte Carlo simulation and saved as CSV files per (building_type, cindex) combination. This is computationally expensive and disabled by default. Default is False.

This class represents the explicit damage ratio. It inherits from the BaseDamageRatio class.

ResistanceValues: dict[str, np.ndarray] A dictionary that holds the resistance values for each component. The keys are the component types and the values are numpy arrays of resistance values.

post_init(): This method is called after the class is instantiated. It initializes the ResistanceValues attribute and calls the fn_damage_ratio_wind() method.

fn_damage_ratio_wind(): This method calculates the damage ratio for each component. The damage ratio is calculated as the number of resistance values that are equal to 0 divided by the total number of resistance values. For RC and RS components, there is a threshold of 35%. If the damage ratio is greater than 35%, then the component is considered to be totaled. For walls, a new damage ratio calculation is used. The wall is considered to be failed if any of the four walls fail. If two walls fail, then the wall is considered to be totaled.

docs.title: CHEERSafe Demo: Complete Hurricane Damage Analysis Workflow¶
docs.text: This notebook demonstrates the complete workflow for hurricane damage and loss assessment using the CHEERSafe package. We'll walk through each step from initial setup to final visualization of results.

docs.title: Prerequisites¶
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • CHEERSafe package installed
  • Required input files (building geometry, etc.)

docs.title: Setup and Environment Configuration¶
docs.text: First, we'll set up the notebook environment with automatic reloading for development.

docs.title: System Configuration¶
docs.text: Let's check the available CPU cores for parallel processing configuration.

docs.title: Package Configuration and Imports¶
docs.text:
Configure the analysis parameters and import required modules. The configuration allows you to customize:

  • NUM_OF_WORKERS: Number of parallel workers for computation
  • NUM_OF_ITERATIONS: Number of Monte Carlo iterations
  • INPUTS_PATH: Directory containing input files
  • OUTPUTS_PATH: Directory for output files

docs.title: Initialize Core Components¶
docs.text:
Set up the building inventory and statistical analysis tools:

  • BuildingInventory: Manages building data and configurations
  • Covariance: Handles covariance calculations for uncertainty analysis
  • Sampling: Provides sampling methods for Monte Carlo simulation

docs.title: Create Main Analysis Engine¶
docs.text: Initialize the damage probability calculation engine with our configured components.

docs.title: Configure Analysis Parameters¶
docs.text:
Specify which building types and resistance indices to process in this analysis:

  • Building Type 2: Specific building classification
  • Resistance Index 46: Specific structural resistance category

docs.title: Run Damage Probability Analysis¶
docs.text: Execute the main damage probability calculation. This step performs Monte Carlo simulations to calculate damage probabilities under various loading conditions.

docs.title: Aggregate Results¶
docs.text: Collect and aggregate the calculated probabilities for further analysis.

docs.title: Results Analysis and Visualization¶
docs.text: Use the analysis module to visualize and interpret the calculated damage probabilities.

docs.title: Generate Analysis Plots¶
docs.text: Create comprehensive plots showing damage probability relationships and fragility curves.

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text:
This notebook demonstrated the complete CHEERSafe workflow:

  1. Setup: Environment configuration and package imports
  2. Initialization: Building inventory and statistical tools setup
  3. Configuration: Analysis parameters and building type selection
  4. Calculation: Monte Carlo damage probability analysis
  5. Visualization: Results analysis and plotting

The generated plots show the relationship between wind speeds, structural parameters, and damage probabilities, providing insights for hurricane risk assessment and mitigation planning.

docs.text:

  • Adjust the number of iterations for different accuracy/speed trade-offs
  • Explore the API documentation for advanced customization options

Configure the analysis parameters and import required modules.

Key Configuration for This Demo:

  • EXPORT_DETAILED_DAMAGE_RATIOS = True: Enables export of detailed component-level damage ratios to CSV

When enabled, the following columns are exported per (building_type, cindex) combination:

  • m: Building type identifier
  • c: Component configuration index
  • wind_orientation_index: Wind orientation index
  • wind_speed_index: Wind speed index
  • flood_depth_index: Flood depth index
  • dr_total: Total building damage ratio
  • dr_explicit: Explicit damage ratio (wind components)
  • dr_implicit: Implicit damage ratio (interior + flood)
  • dr_exp_wind_RC: Roof Coverings explicit damage ratio
  • dr_exp_wind_RS: Roof Sheathings explicit damage ratio
  • dr_exp_wind_RWC: Roof-Wall Connections explicit damage ratio
  • dr_exp_wind_O: Openings explicit damage ratio
  • dr_exp_wind_W: Walls explicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_wind_I: Interior implicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_wind_E: Electrical implicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_wind_M: Mechanical implicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_wind_P: Plumbing implicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_flood: Flood implicit damage ratio

docs.text: This guide will help you install the cheersafe package on your system.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Ensure that you have Python and pip installed on your system. You can check this by running the following commands in your terminal:

python --version
pip --version

If you do not have Python or pip installed, please install them first.

docs.title: Installation Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the cheersafe repository to your local machine:
git clone https://github.com/CHEER-Hub/LossModel.git
  1. Navigate to the cloned repository:
cd LossModel
  1. Install the package using pip:
pip install .

docs.title: Optional Dependencies

To install development tools (pytest, pytest-cov, tox):

pip install .[dev]

pip install .[docs]

pip install .[jupyter]

That's it! You have successfully installed the cheersafe package on your system.

from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.damage_probability_calculation import DamageProbabilityCalculation
from cheersafe.inventory import BuildingInventory
from cheersafe.tools.stats import Covariance, Sampling

Config.NUM_OF_ITERATIONS = 5
Config.NUM_OF_WORKERS = 1
Config.INPUTS_PATH = "Inputs"
Config.OUTPUTS_PATH = "Outputs"

inventory = BuildingInventory(buildings_file_name="BuildingGeometry_Old.json")
calculation = DamageProbabilityCalculation(
    BuildingInventory=inventory,
    Sampling=Sampling(),
    Covariance=Covariance(),
)

calculation.set_building_types_to_process([1])
calculation.set_cindex_to_process([1])
calculation.get_average_damage_probability()
probabilities = calculation.aggregate_results()

Config.reset_flags()

docs.title: Key Concepts
docs.text:
• Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=True lets supported classes load their standard input files during initialization.
  • Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS=True lets supported classes calculate derived outputs during initialization.
  • Turn either flag off when you want to load data or assign returned method outputs manually.
  • Most public building and calculation indices in examples are 1-based, while several lower-level arrays use Python's 0-based indexing internally.

docs.title: CHEERSafe Input Manual
docs.text:
This page describes the input files loaded by CHEERSafe at runtime. The runtime JSON and CSV files in Inputs/ are the source of truth. The temporary workbook Inputs/RawData_WithHeaders.xlsx was used here only to recover labels, units, and assumptions for the manual.

Runtime files are authoritative

CHEERSafe calculations load the JSON and CSV files directly. If a workbook value differs from a runtime file, use the runtime file value unless the input file itself is intentionally updated.

Known differences found while preparing this page:

  • BuildingGeometry.json and BuildingGeometry_Old.json contain rounded geometry values relative to the workbook, such as roof pitch and roof dimensions.
  • WindSpeed.json stores metric wind speeds rounded to one decimal place, while the workbook keeps more decimal precision.
  • MeanResistanceCV.json currently stores 0.3 for all component and configuration entries, while the workbook's current resistance sheet shows component-specific CV values.
  • CCRoofGCp.json stores roof zone coefficients [-0.9, -2.1, -2.1]; the workbook's current pressure-coefficient sheet lists roof zone 2 as -1.7.

docs.title: Input Conventions
docs.text:
CHEERSafe expects the standard runtime input files under Config.INPUTS_PATH, which defaults to Inputs. Most input loaders call Utils.from_json, which converts JSON arrays to NumPy arrays. JSON objects, such as Hurricane_ProbWindFlood.json, are returned as dictionaries whose values are arrays after downstream use. The building-value file is a CSV read with pandas.

Many tables include an explicit ID, building type, component configuration, or damage-state number. These values are 1-based in the input files. Internally, Python code often subtracts 1 when indexing arrays, so do not renumber file IDs to zero-based values.

Array shapes in this manual use the following axis names:

Axis Meaning i Spatial zone or inventory index. Runtime regional inputs use 1509 zones. m Building type. CHEERSafe includes 8 building types. c Component or resistance configuration. The full runtime set has 192 configurations. h Hurricane event index. The bundled hurricane input has 97 events. f Flood-depth index. The bundled flood-depth grid has 136 depths. d Damage-state index. Wind has 50 states; flood has 6 states.

docs.title: Building Geometry
docs.text:
BuildingGeometry.json and BuildingGeometry_Old.json share the same schema: 28 rows by 8 building-type columns. Each column is one archetype. Row 1 stores the building type index, and rows 2 through 28 store the attributes used to instantiate Building objects.

BuildingInventory currently defaults to BuildingGeometry_Old.json. Use BuildingGeometry.json explicitly when you want the newer geometry table.

Row Building attribute Unit or code Meaning 1 BldgType ID Building type index, 1 through 8. 2 Story 1 or 2 Number of stories. 3 Material 1 wood, 2 URM Wall/building material code. 4 WallFloorCon_FrontBack count Wall-floor connections on front and back walls. 5 WallFloorCon_Side count Wall-floor connections on side walls. 6 BldgLength ft Building length. 7 BldgWidth ft Building width. 8 MeanRoofHeight ft Mean roof height. 9 WallHeight ft Wall height. 10 OpeningFront count Front windows. 11 OpeningBack count Back windows. 12 OpeningSideR count Regular side windows. 13 OpeningSideH count High side windows. 14 OpeningLength ft Window length, vertical dimension. 15 OpeningWidth ft Window width, horizontal dimension. 16 DoorFront count Front doors. 17 DoorGarage count Garage doors. 18 DoorBack count Back doors. 19 RoofShape 1 hip, 2 gable Roof-shape code. 20 RoofPitchDegree degrees Roof pitch angle. 21 RoofPitch_r rise/run Roof pitch as a ratio. 22 RoofHeight ft Roof height. 23 RoofWidth ft Roof width. 24 HipRidgeLength ft Hip ridge length. 25 HipRidgeAngle degrees Hip ridge angle. 26 TrussSpacing ft Roof truss spacing. 27 SheathingLength ft Sheathing panel length. 28 SheathingWidth ft Sheathing panel width.

Current and old geometry

The workbook labels BuildingGeometry_Old as the geometry from Jiazhen's dissertation. BuildingGeometry follows the same schema but changes the opening counts, especially the window counts. The runtime code still uses the old file by default unless a different buildings_file_name is passed.

docs.title: Mean Resistance Values And CVs
docs.text:
MeanResistanceValue.json and MeanResistanceCV.json both use 10 component rows and 3 resistance-configuration columns. Empty workbook cells are stored as 0 in MeanResistanceValue.json. Runtime component combinations choose one of these configuration columns for each component family.

Row Component Short name Unit for mean resistance Configuration columns 1 Roof cover RC psf 1, 2 2 Roof sheathing RS psf 1, 2 3 Roof-to-wall connection, side RWC lbs 1, 2 4 Roof-to-wall connection, gable RWC lbs 1, 2 5 Opening, door O psf 1, 2, 3 6 Opening, garage door O psf 1, 2, 3 7 Opening, window O psf 1, 2, 3 8 Wall, shear W lb/linear ft 1, 2 9 Wall, uplift W lb/ft 1, 2 10 Wall, out-of-plane W lbs 1, 2

Runtime mean resistance values are:

Component Config 1 Config 2 Config 3 Roof cover 50 70 0 Roof sheathing 100 225 0 RWC side 1400 2825 0 RWC gable 1400 2825 0 Door 75 150 113 Garage door 50 75 75 Window 55 110 82.5 Wall shear 1100 1100 0 Wall uplift 1000 1000 0 Wall out-of-plane 2000 3000 0

Resistance CV reconciliation

MeanResistanceCV.json currently contains 0.3 in every row and column. Treat that as the value used by CHEERSafe until the JSON file is changed. Do not infer the runtime CVs from the workbook's current resistance sheet.

docs.title: Component Combinations
docs.text:
Component combinations define which resistance configuration applies to each component family.

File Shape Columns or axes Notes ComponentCombination_All.json [192, 6] RC, RS, RWC, O, W, F Full compact set. The first five columns select wind resistance configurations; F selects the flood probability configuration. ComponentCombination_Hip.json [24, 10] Expanded hip-roof combination rows Used when processing hip-roof building types. ComponentCombination_Gable.json [48, 10] Expanded gable-roof combination rows Used when processing gable-roof building types.

The compact configuration IDs are 1-based. For example, a row beginning [1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 1] means roof cover config 1, roof sheathing config 1, roof-to-wall connection config 2, opening config 3, wall config 1, and flood config 1.

docs.title: Wind, Flood, And Orientation Grids
docs.text:
WindSpeed.json, FloodDepth.json, and WindOrientation.json define the discrete hazard grid used in probability and loss calculations.

File Columns Runtime range WindSpeed.json ID, WindSpeed (mph), WindSpeed (m/s) 25 rows, from 0 mph to 215 mph. Metric speeds are rounded to one decimal place. FloodDepth.json ID, FloodDepth (inch), FloodDepth (meter) 136 rows, from 0 inches to 270 inches. WindOrientation.json ID, Angle (degrees) 8 rows: 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, and 315 degrees.

The ID column is part of the file format. It is not the same as a zero-based Python array index.

docs.title: Wind Pressure Coefficients
docs.text:
Pressure coefficients are dimensionless and are loaded by the loading and failure-check classes.

File Runtime values Meaning CCRoofGCp.json [-0.9, -2.1, -2.1] Roof component-and-cladding GCp values for zones 1, 2, and 3. CCWallGCp.json [1, -1.4, -1.1, -0.8] Wall component-and-cladding GCp values for windward, side leading edge, side, and leeward walls. MWFRSCp.json [0.8, -0.3, -0.7, -0.25, -0.57, -0.9, -0.5, -0.3] Main wind force resisting system coefficients for building surfaces 1 through 8.

docs.title: Damage States
docs.text:
DamageState.json defines wind damage states as pairs of damage-state index and damage ratio. The bundled file has 50 states. It starts at damage ratio 0, increments by 0.004 through the early states, and ends at damage state 50 with damage ratio 1.4.

DamageState_Flood.json defines flood damage-state thresholds as pairs of damage-state index and lower damage-range percent:

Flood damage state Lower damage range (%) 1 0 2 1 3 11 4 21 5 31 6 41

docs.title: Flood Damage-State Probabilities
docs.text:
ProbDS_Flood.json has shape [8, 4, 136, 6].

Axis Meaning 1 Building type m, values 1 through 8. 2 Flood configuration F, values 1 through 4 from ComponentCombination_All.json. 3 Flood-depth row from FloodDepth.json. 4 Flood damage state from DamageState_Flood.json.

Each [m, F, f, :] slice is a probability vector over the 6 flood damage states. Damage-ratio code converts the selected vector to a cumulative distribution before sampling.

docs.title: Replacement Ratios
docs.text:
ReplacementRatio.json has shape [8, 9]. Rows are building types 1 through 8, and columns are replacement-cost shares by component.

Column Component 1 Roof cover (RC) 2 Roof sheathing (RS) 3 Roof-to-wall connection (RWC) 4 Opening (O) 5 Wall (W) 6 Interior 7 Electrical 8 Mechanical 9 Plumbing

The workbook includes a Sum column for checking totals, but the runtime JSON stores only the 9 component-share columns. Current row totals are about 1.10 or 1.11 depending on building type.

docs.title: Hurricane Probability, Wind, Flood, And Flood Ratio
docs.text:
Hurricane_ProbWindFlood.json is a JSON object with four keys:

Key Shape Meaning Hurricane_WindSpeed [1509, 97] Wind speed by zone and hurricane event. Hurricane_FloodDepth [1509, 97] Flood depth by zone and hurricane event. Hurricane_FloodRatio [1509, 97] Flood-exposed share or ratio by zone and hurricane event. Hurricane_Prob [97, 2] Hurricane event probability table.

Loss estimators adjust wind and flood arrays by peril. For WIND, flood depth is set to zero; for FLOOD, wind speed is set to zero.

docs.title: Regional Inventory
docs.text: X_imc.json has shape [1509, 8, 192]. It stores regional exposure counts by zone i, building type m, and component configuration c. RegionalLossEstimator broadcasts this inventory against component losses and sums over i, m, and c to produce hurricane-level regional losses.

docs.title: Building Values CSV
docs.text:
Building_imc_Component_ZTRAXPropValueSample.csv is the building-level exposure and value file used by BuildingLossEstimator. The bundled CSV has 931902 data rows and these columns:

Column Meaning i Source zone or record group identifier. m Building type. c Component/resistance configuration. RC Roof cover configuration. RS Roof sheathing configuration. RWC Roof-to-wall connection configuration. O Opening configuration. W Wall configuration. F Flood configuration. num_stories Number of stories. total_value Total property value. improvement_value Structure or improvement value used for building loss. ind_1509 Regional zone index used to look up hurricane wind and flood data.

For building-level loss estimates, m, c, ind_1509, and improvement_value are the key fields used directly in the loss loop. Keep component configuration fields consistent with ComponentCombination_All.json when preparing a custom CSV.

docs.title: Config
docs.text: cheersafe.config.Config is a dataclass used as global class-level runtime configuration. Import it when you need to select input/output directories, switch between automatic and manual workflows, set simulation sizes, or reset a session after changing global flags.

docs.title: Purpose And When To Use
docs.text:
Use Config before constructing CHEERSafe objects. Most classes read the class attributes during initialization, so changing a flag after an object is created does not retroactively load datasets or calculate missing attributes unless the object exposes an explicit method such as update_outputs().

Config.reset_flags() restores the package defaults and is useful in notebooks, tests, and examples where previous cells may have changed global state.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Config has no instance inputs. Set class attributes directly.

Attribute Default Unit or meaning Used by AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS True Run calculation methods during object initialization. Building, loads, damage ratio, and analysis calculators. AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS True Load file-backed datasets during object initialization. BuildingInventory, loads, damage probability, analysis, and loss workflows. INPUTS_PATH "Inputs" Directory containing runtime JSON/CSV input files. Dataset loaders and inventory loaders. OUTPUTS_PATH "Outputs" Directory for generated pickle/CSV outputs. Damage probability and loss output workflows. NUM_OF_ITERATIONS 3000 Monte Carlo iterations. Damage probability calculation. NUM_OF_WORKERS 4 Parallel jobs. Joblib-backed damage probability calculation. NUM_OF_WORKERS_SAMPLING 1 Workers passed to SciPy Latin hypercube sampling. Sampling.generate_lhs_samples_*. RANDOM_SEED 42 Default deterministic seed. Sampling helpers. EXPORT_DETAILED_DAMAGE_RATIOS False Export component-level detailed damage-ratio CSV files. Damage probability calculation.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text: Config.reset_flags() mutates the class attributes above and returns None. The class itself does not produce arrays or files. Other modules read its values when they load data, run calculations, or write outputs.

docs.title: AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, file-backed classes load their datasets during initialization. For example, BuildingInventory() reads Config.INPUTS_PATH / buildings_file_name.

With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = False, those classes are created without loading their datasets. Call the relevant loader manually, such as inventory.instantiate_buildings_from_json().

Config itself is never file-backed, so this flag does not change how Config is created.

docs.title: AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, calculation classes that support automatic execution compute their derived outputs during initialization. For inventory, each Building computes PanelCoordinate, NumPanel, ConnectionCoordinate, and NumConnection when it is instantiated.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = False, calculation outputs are left unset until you call the corresponding method and assign or pass along the returned values.

Config itself has no calculation methods controlled by this flag.

docs.title: Minimal Automatic Example
docs.text:
Run from the repository root before package installation:

PYTHONPATH=src python3 - <<'PY'
from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.inventory import BuildingInventory

Config.reset_flags()
Config.INPUTS_PATH = "Inputs"

inventory = BuildingInventory()
print(len(inventory.buildings))
print(inventory.buildings[0].PanelCoordinate.shape)

Config.reset_flags()
PY

docs.title: Minimal Manual-Control Example
docs.text:
PYTHONPATH=src python3 - <<'PY'
from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.inventory import BuildingInventory

Config.reset_flags()
Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = False
Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = False

inventory = BuildingInventory()
print(hasattr(inventory, "buildings"))

inventory.instantiate_buildings_from_json()
building = inventory.buildings[0]

panel_coordinate, num_panel = building.fn_panel_coordinate()
connection_coordinate, num_connection = building.fn_connection_coordinate()

print(panel_coordinate.shape, num_panel.tolist())
print(connection_coordinate.shape, num_connection)

Config.reset_flags()
PY

docs.title: Damage Probability Analysis
docs.text: Use this module after damage probability calculation has produced an aggregated probability dictionary. The analysis classes turn ProbDS_wfd arrays into vulnerability curves, fragility curves, saved JSON, and matplotlib figures.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Page Use when VulnerabilityCalculator You need expected damage ratio versus wind speed for one building type and resistance configuration. FragilityCalculator You need probability of exceeding damage-state thresholds versus wind speed. DamageProbabilityAnalysis You want vulnerability and fragility outputs from one convenience class.

docs.title: Shared Inputs
docs.text:
Input Default Shape Units or indexing prob_ds_file_path Outputs/ProbDS_wfd_dictMaxIter{NUM_OF_ITERATIONS}_aggregated.pkl dict[(m, c), array] Keys use building type and 1-based resistance/configuration id. Inputs/WindSpeed.json runtime file [25, 3] id, mph, m/s; plots use mph. Inputs/FloodDepth.json runtime file [136, 3] id, inches, meters. Inputs/DamageState.json runtime file [50, 2] damage-state id, damage ratio. building_type 1 scalar Building type key m. resistance_type 1 scalar Component/resistance key c, 1-based.

The current calculations use flood-depth index 0 for wind-only vulnerability and fragility curves.

docs.title: Configuration Behavior
docs.text:
Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=True loads the probability dictionary, wind grid, flood grid, and damage-state table during initialization. With False, call the load_* methods before running calculations.

Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS=True computes outputs during construction for VulnerabilityCalculator and FragilityCalculator; DamageProbabilityAnalysis inherits both behaviors. With False, call calculation methods manually and assign returned values if you want them stored on the instance.

docs.title: Minimal Examples
docs.text:
Automatic calculation:

from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.damage_probability_analysis import DamageProbabilityAnalysis

Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True
Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True

analysis = DamageProbabilityAnalysis(
    building_type=1,
    resistance_type=1,
    prob_ds_file_path="Outputs/ProbDS_wfd_dictMaxIter50_aggregated.pkl",
)
results = analysis.generate_analysis()

Manual control:

from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.damage_probability_analysis import DamageProbabilityAnalysis

Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = False
Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = False

analysis = DamageProbabilityAnalysis(
    building_type=1,
    resistance_type=1,
    prob_ds_file_path="Outputs/ProbDS_wfd_dictMaxIter50_aggregated.pkl",
)
analysis.load_prob_damage_states()
analysis.load_wind_speed()
analysis.load_flood_depth()
analysis.load_damage_state()

analysis.expected_damage_ratio, analysis.vulnerability_curve = (
    analysis.calculate_vulnerability_curve()
)
analysis.fragility_curves = analysis.calculate_fragility_curves()

docs.title: DamageProbabilityAnalysis
docs.text: DamageProbabilityAnalysis is the convenience class that combines vulnerability and fragility analysis for one (building_type, resistance_type) pair. Use it when you want both curve families and optional saved plots or JSON output.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Inputs are inherited from FragilityCalculator:

Input Default Notes prob_ds_file_path aggregated pickle in Outputs/ Must contain (building_type, resistance_type) as a key. building_type 1 Building type key m. resistance_type 1 Resistance/configuration key c, 1-based. wind_scale_lines [74, 95, 110, 130, 157] Plot guide lines in mph. ds_thresholds [0.03, 0.09, 0.22, 0.46] Damage-ratio thresholds. output_dir Outputs Directory used by save_analysis_results().

The required file dependencies are the aggregated probability pickle plus Inputs/WindSpeed.json, Inputs/FloodDepth.json, and Inputs/DamageState.json.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
Method Returns Side effects generate_analysis() Dictionary with vulnerability_curve and fragility_curves. None. save_analysis_results(file_name=None) Path to saved JSON file. Writes JSON under output_dir. plot_analysis_results(save_path=None) List of two matplotlib figures. Shows plots and optionally writes PNG files.

When AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS=True, inherited attributes expected_damage_ratio, vulnerability_curve, and fragility_curves are available immediately after construction.

docs.title: Configuration Behavior
docs.text:
AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=True loads all required data during construction. AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=False requires manual calls to load_prob_damage_states(), load_wind_speed(), load_flood_depth(), and load_damage_state().

AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS=True computes both vulnerability and fragility outputs during construction through the parent classes. With False, compute and assign outputs manually before calling generate_analysis() or save/plot helpers.

docs.title: Minimal Examples
docs.text:

from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.damage_probability_analysis import DamageProbabilityAnalysis

Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True
Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True

analysis = DamageProbabilityAnalysis(
    building_type=1,
    resistance_type=1,
    prob_ds_file_path="Outputs/ProbDS_wfd_dictMaxIter50_aggregated.pkl",
)
summary = analysis.generate_analysis()
json_path = analysis.save_analysis_results()

Manual control:

from cheersafe.damage_probability_analysis import DamageProbabilityAnalysis

Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = False
Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = False

analysis = DamageProbabilityAnalysis(
    building_type=1,
    resistance_type=1,
    prob_ds_file_path="Outputs/ProbDS_wfd_dictMaxIter50_aggregated.pkl",

analysis.load_flood_depth()

    analysis.calculate_vulnerability_curve()

analysis.fragility_curves = analysis.calculate_fragility_curves()

docs.title: FragilityCalculator
docs.text: FragilityCalculator extends vulnerability analysis with exceedance-style fragility curves. Use it when you need probability curves for grouped damage states at selected damage-ratio thresholds.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
FragilityCalculator uses the same probability dictionary, wind grid, flood grid, and damage-state table as VulnerabilityCalculator.

Additional inputs:

Input Default Units or indexing ds_thresholds [0.03, 0.09, 0.22, 0.46] Damage-ratio thresholds, unitless fractions. line_styles built-in list Matplotlib style strings for plotting.

The calculation uses prob_damage_states[(building_type, resistance_type)][:, 0, :], so flood-depth index 0 is used for wind fragility.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
calculate_fragility_curves() returns a dictionary:

Key Shape Meaning wind_speed [wind] Wind speeds in mph. DS0 [wind] Probability associated with exceeding the lowest damage group. DS1, DS2, ... [wind] Curves derived from ds_thresholds.

plot_fragility_curves(save_path=None) returns a matplotlib figure and optionally writes an image file.

docs.title: Configuration Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=True, all datasets load at construction. With False, call the inherited load_* methods first.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS=True, construction computes inherited vulnerability outputs and fragility_curves. With False, call calculate_vulnerability_curve() and calculate_fragility_curves() manually.

docs.title: VulnerabilityCalculator
docs.text: VulnerabilityCalculator converts damage-state probabilities into an expected damage-ratio curve for one building type and one resistance configuration. Use it when you need a wind vulnerability curve rather than the full probability surface.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Type Units or indexing prob_ds_file_path str Pickle containing dict[(m, c), ProbDS_wfd]. building_type int Building type key m; default 1. resistance_type int Resistance/configuration key c; default 1, 1-based. wind_scale_lines list[int] Optional wind-speed guide lines in mph.

Loaded arrays:

Value Shape Notes prob_damage_states[(m, c)] [wind, flood, damage_state] Usually produced by DamageProbabilityCalculation.aggregate_results(). wind_speed [25, 3] Vulnerability curve uses column 1, mph. damage_state [50, 2] Expected damage ratio uses column 1.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
calculate_vulnerability_curve() returns (expected_damage_ratio, vulnerability_curve).

Output Shape Meaning expected_damage_ratio [wind] Dot product of wind-only damage-state probabilities and damage ratios. vulnerability_curve["wind_speed"] [wind] Wind speeds in mph. vulnerability_curve["expected_damage_ratio"] [wind] Expected damage ratio.

plot_vulnerability_curve(save_path=None) returns a matplotlib figure and optionally saves it to save_path.

docs.title: Configuration Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=True, datasets load during initialization. With False, load them manually before calling calculate_vulnerability_curve().

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS=True, initialization assigns expected_damage_ratio and vulnerability_curve. With False, the method returns those values and the caller decides whether to assign them.

docs.title: Damage Probability Calculation
docs.text: Use this module to generate CHEERSafe damage-state probability surfaces from building inventories, component resistance samples, wind speeds, flood depths, and wind orientations. It is the upstream producer for vulnerability, fragility, and loss-estimation workflows.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Page Use when DamageCalculator You need helper methods for selecting component combinations, mapping resistance parameters, or converting iteration damage ratios to damage-state probabilities. DamageProbabilityCalculation You need the full Monte Carlo workflow that writes ProbDS_wfd_m{m}_c{c}_iter{n}.pkl files and optionally aggregates them. DamageRatioExporter You enable detailed damage-ratio CSV export during probability calculations.

docs.title: Shared Inputs
docs.text:
Most classes inherit the dataset loaders from the base calculation class and expect these runtime inputs under Config.INPUTS_PATH, normally Inputs/:

File Shape Units or indexing Purpose ProbDS_Flood.json [8, 4, 136, 6] building type, flood configuration, flood-depth index, flood damage state Flood damage-state probabilities. DamageState.json [50, 2] 1-based damage-state id, damage ratio Wind damage-state bins used to classify simulated damage ratios. WindSpeed.json [25, 3] id, mph, m/s Wind grid. Calculation uses column 2 as mph. WindOrientation.json [8, 2] id, degrees Orientation grid. MeanResistanceCV.json [10, 3] component row, resistance config Resistance coefficients of variation. MeanResistanceValue.json [10, 3] component row, resistance config Mean resistance values. Units depend on component family. ComponentCombination_Hip.json [24, 10] 1-based config values Hip-roof combinations. ComponentCombination_Gable.json [48, 10] 1-based config values Gable-roof combinations. ComponentCombination_All.json [192, 6] RC, RS, RWC, O, W, F Full compact configuration table.

The main workflow also needs initialized BuildingInventory, Sampling, and Covariance objects.

docs.title: Configuration Behavior
docs.text:
Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=True loads the shared datasets during initialization. With False, instantiate the class and call the load_* methods before using helper or workflow methods that rely on those arrays.

DamageProbabilityCalculation does not run the Monte Carlo workflow in __post_init__; call get_average_damage_probability() explicitly. Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS still affects downstream objects created inside the workflow, such as loading and damage-ratio classes.

Current nuance: DamageProbabilityCalculation.__post_init__ sizes a compatibility IterationResult array from WindSpeeds and ProbDS_Flood. Because of that, constructing this specific class with AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=False is not a working manual-load pattern unless those attributes are supplied before __post_init__ runs. Use DamageCalculator for manual helper work, or keep auto-loading enabled and control execution by calling workflow methods explicitly.

docs.text: DamageCalculator is the shared helper layer for damage probability calculation. Use it when you need to inspect component-combination tables, build per-component resistance vectors, or convert Monte Carlo damage-ratio iterations into damage-state probabilities without running the full building inventory workflow.

docs.title: DamageProbabilityCalculation
docs.text: DamageProbabilityCalculation is the full Monte Carlo engine for generating damage-state probability arrays by building type and component configuration. Use it after inventory, loading, damage-ratio, and resistance inputs are ready.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Constructor inputs:

Input Type Notes BuildingInventory BuildingInventory Supplies buildings; each building must already have inventory outputs such as panels and connections available. Sampling Sampling Generates Latin-hypercube resistance samples and derived random seeds. Covariance Covariance Builds covariance matrices from component means and CVs. building_types_to_process list[int] or None Optional filter. Values are building-type ids such as 1. cindex_to_process list[int] or None Optional filter. Public cIndex values are 1-based.

Loaded file inputs are listed in the module overview. The workflow also creates LoadingAndFailureCheck and DamageRatioCalculation objects for each sampled condition, so their required inventory, pressure coefficient, replacement ratio, and damage-ratio inputs must be available too.

Key indexing and shapes:

Value Shape Notes wind grid len(WindSpeeds) Bundled input has 25 wind-speed rows. flood grid ProbDS_Flood.shape[2] Bundled input has 136 flood-depth rows. damage states len(DamageStates) Bundled input has 50 states. per-run output [wind, flood, damage_state] Saved for each (building_type, cIndex). aggregate output dict[(m, c), array] Keys are integer building type and 1-based cIndex.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
Method Returns Files or state set_building_types_to_process(building_types) None Stores the building-type filter. set_cindex_to_process(cindices) None Stores the 1-based component-index filter. Rejects values below 1. process_single_iteration(...) (iter_results, detailed_results) No persistent state. process_component_combination(building, ComponentCombination, cIndex) (m, cIndex, ProbDS_wfd) or None Writes ProbDS_wfd_m{m}_c{cIndex}_iter{NUM_OF_ITERATIONS}.pkl; may write detailed CSV. get_available_building_types() list[int] None. get_available_cindices() list[int] None. get_average_damage_probability() True Writes one pickle per processed (m, cIndex). aggregate_results(output_dir=None) dict[(int, int), np.ndarray] Sets ProbDS_wfd_dict and writes ProbDS_wfd_dictMaxIter{NUM_OF_ITERATIONS}_aggregated.pkl.

Detailed CSV export is controlled by Config.EXPORT_DETAILED_DAMAGE_RATIOS. When enabled, files are named DetailedDR_m{m}_c{cIndex}_iter{NUM_OF_ITERATIONS}.csv.

docs.title: Configuration Behavior
docs.text:
Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=True loads shared probability-calculation datasets during initialization. With False, call all required load_* methods before running workflow methods. Current limitation: this class also creates IterationResult in __post_init__ from WindSpeeds and ProbDS_Flood, so a plain construction with AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=False raises before manual loaders can be called. Keep auto-loading enabled for this class unless you are subclassing or otherwise pre-populating those attributes before __post_init__.

DamageProbabilityCalculation.__post_init__ initializes compatibility storage but does not call get_average_damage_probability(). Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS affects downstream CHEERSafe objects constructed during the run.

docs.title: DamageRatioExporter
docs.text: DamageRatioExporter collects component-level damage-ratio records during a Monte Carlo damage-probability run and exports iteration-averaged CSV tables. Use it directly for custom post-processing, or let DamageProbabilityCalculation create it when Config.EXPORT_DETAILED_DAMAGE_RATIOS=True.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Constructor inputs:

Input Type Units or indexing building_type int CHEERSafe building type id. cindex int Public component configuration id; 1-based. collected_data list[dict] Optional existing records. Defaults to an empty list.

collect_detailed_ratios() expects a computed DamageRatioCalculation object with total, explicit wind, implicit wind, and implicit flood damage-ratio values available. Damage ratios are unitless fractions.

add_record() takes zero-based wind-orientation, wind-speed, and flood-depth indices plus the Monte Carlo iteration number.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
Method Returns Side effects collect_detailed_ratios(damage_ratios) dict[str, float] with standardized damage-ratio columns. None. add_record(...) None Appends one record to collected_data. aggregate_and_save_to_csv(output_dir=None) CSV path, or "" when there is no data. Writes DetailedDR_m{building_type}_c{cindex}_iter{NUM_OF_ITERATIONS}.csv. clear() None Clears collected_data.

CSV rows are grouped by m, c, wind_orientation_index, wind_speed_index, and flood_depth_index; damage-ratio columns are averaged over iteration.

docs.title: Damage Ratio Calculation
docs.text:
The cheersafe.damage_ratio_calculation classes convert final component failure states into explicit wind damage ratios, implicit wind damage ratios, implicit flood damage ratios, and weighted building damage ratios.

Use these classes after a cheersafe.loads.LoadingAndFailureCheck object has produced final loads and final resistances for one building, component configuration, flood depth, wind orientation, wind speed, and resistance sample.

Related API: Damage Ratio Calculation API Related notebook: Fragility Curve Calculation with Detailed Damage Ratio Analysis

docs.title: Class Pages
docs.text:
• ExplicitDamageRatio: component-level wind damage ratios for roof, openings, walls, and roof-wall connections.
  • ImplicitDamageRatio: interior, utility, and flood damage ratios.
  • DamageRatioCalculation: weighted building-level explicit, implicit, and total damage ratios.

docs.title: Shared Inputs
docs.text:
All classes require:

  • Building: a cheersafe.inventory.Building. Damage-ratio weighting uses Building.BldgType; implicit wind also uses Building.Story.
  • FailureChecks: a cheersafe.loads.LoadingAndFailureCheck or compatible object with get_final_resistance().
  • ComponentConfigurationIndex: zero-based row index into Inputs/ComponentCombination_All.json; valid range is 0 to 191 for the current dataset.
  • FloodDepthIndex: zero-based row index into the flood-depth dimension of ProbDS_Flood; the current probability file has 136 flood-depth rows.
  • Optional rng: seed, NumPy generator, or compatible random source used by stochastic implicit damage methods.

docs.title: Dataset Loading
docs.text:
With Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, BaseDamageRatio.__post_init__ loads:

  • Inputs/ProbDS_Flood.json, shape (8, 4, 136, 6).
  • Inputs/ComponentCombination_All.json, shape (192, 6).
  • Inputs/DamageState_Flood.json, shape (6, 2).
  • Inputs/ReplacementRatio.json, shape (8, 9).

With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = False, call the load_* methods or assign the arrays/dictionaries before executing damage-ratio methods that use them.

docs.title: Method Execution
docs.text:
With Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, constructors calculate and assign class outputs. With it disabled, call methods manually and assign returned values explicitly.

import numpy as np
from cheersafe.damage_ratio_calculation import DamageRatioCalculation
from cheersafe.inventory import BuildingInventory
from cheersafe.loads import LoadingAndFailureCheck
from cheersafe.tools import Utils

building = BuildingInventory(buildings_file_name="BuildingGeometry.json").buildings[0]
mean = Utils.from_json("Inputs/MeanResistanceValue.json")
failure = LoadingAndFailureCheck(
    np.full(sum(building.NumPanel), mean[1, 0]),
    np.full(sum(building.NumPanel), mean[0, 0]),
    np.full(sum(building.NumConnection), mean[2, 0]),
    np.full(building.DoorFront + building.DoorBack + building.DoorGarage
            + building.OpeningFront + building.OpeningBack
            + 2 * (building.OpeningSideR + building.OpeningSideH), mean[3, 0]),
    np.full(12, mean[4, 0]),
    building,
    0,
    50,
)
ratio = DamageRatioCalculation(building, failure, 0, 0, rng=1234)
print(ratio.get_building_damage_ratio())

docs.title: DamageRatioCalculation
docs.text:
DamageRatioCalculation is the main damage-ratio workflow class. It calculates explicit component damage ratios, implicit wind and flood damage ratios, and replacement-ratio-weighted building damage ratios.

Use it after LoadingAndFailureCheck when you need the final building damage ratio for one scenario.

Related API: Damage Ratio Calculation API Related notebook: Fragility Curve Calculation with Detailed Damage Ratio Analysis

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Building: cheersafe.inventory.Building.
  • FailureChecks: cheersafe.loads.LoadingAndFailureCheck.
  • ComponentConfigurationIndex: zero-based row index into ComponentCombination_All.
  • FloodDepthIndex: zero-based row index in the flood-depth dimension.
  • Optional rng: seed or generator for stochastic implicit damage.

File dependencies with automatic dataset loading:

  • Inputs/ComponentCombination_All.json, shape (192, 6).
  • Inputs/ProbDS_Flood.json, shape (8, 4, 136, 6).
  • Inputs/DamageState_Flood.json, shape (6, 2).
  • Inputs/ReplacementRatio.json, shape (8, 9).

ReplacementRatio is converted to a dictionary keyed by one-based building type. Component keys are "Roof Coverings", "Roof Sheathings", "Roof-Wall Connections", "Openings", "Walls", "Interior", "Electrical", "Mechanical", and "Plumbing".

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
Automatic attributes are inherited:

  • ExplicitDamageRatioWind: explicit wind component ratios.
  • ImplicitDamageRatioWind: implicit wind component ratios.
  • ImplicitDamageRatioFlood: implicit flood scalar ratio.
  • tempProbDS_Flood: cumulative flood probabilities for the selected component configuration.

Getter returns:

  • get_damage_ratio_wind_explicit() -> float: replacement-ratio-weighted explicit wind damage.
  • get_damage_ratio_wind_implicit() -> float: replacement-ratio-weighted implicit wind damage.
  • get_damage_ratio_flood_implicit() -> float: flood damage scalar.
  • get_damage_ratio_explicit() -> float: currently the same as explicit wind damage.
  • get_damage_ratio_implicit() -> float: combined wind/flood implicit damage using min(max(wind, flood) + 0.5 * min(wind, flood), 1).
  • get_building_damage_ratio() -> float: explicit plus implicit damage.

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, all needed damage-ratio datasets are loaded during construction. With it disabled, call load_ProbDS_Flood(), load_component_combination_all(), load_DS_Flood(), and load_replacement_ratio() or assign equivalent attributes before methods use them.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, all explicit and implicit component ratios are populated during construction. With it disabled, execute the methods manually before calling the building-level getters.

docs.title: ExplicitDamageRatio
docs.text:
ExplicitDamageRatio calculates wind damage ratios for components represented directly in the final resistance dictionary: roof coverings, roof sheathings, roof-wall connections, openings, and walls.

Use it when you need component-level explicit wind damage ratios without the implicit interior, utility, or flood calculations.

Related API: Damage Ratio Calculation API Related notebook: Fragility Curve Calculation with Detailed Damage Ratio Analysis

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Building: cheersafe.inventory.Building.
  • FailureChecks: object with get_final_resistance() -> dict[str, np.ndarray].
  • ComponentConfigurationIndex: zero-based component-configuration row. Required by the base class even though explicit wind ratios do not use it directly.
  • FloodDepthIndex: zero-based flood-depth row. Required by the base class even though explicit wind ratios do not use it directly.

FailureChecks.get_final_resistance() must return these keys:

  • "Roof Coverings" and "Roof Sheathings": shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • "Roof-Wall Connections": shape (sum(Building.NumConnection),).
  • "Openings": total opening count.
  • "Walls": shape (12,), reshaped internally as (4, 3) with Fortran order.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
With automatic execution:

  • ResistanceValues: final resistance dictionary from FailureChecks.
  • ExplicitDamageRatioWind: dict[str, float] keyed by component name.

fn_damage_ratio_wind() returns the explicit wind dictionary. A component ratio is generally the fraction of resistance entries equal to zero. Roof coverings and roof sheathings are treated as total loss when their ratio exceeds 0.35. Walls are evaluated by wall side: one failed side gives 0.25; two or more failed sides give 1.0.

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, base damage-ratio datasets are loaded even though this class only needs the final resistance dictionary for fn_damage_ratio_wind().

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, the explicit dictionary is calculated during construction. With it disabled, ResistanceValues is still set by __post_init__, but call and assign fn_damage_ratio_wind() yourself.

docs.title: ImplicitDamageRatio
docs.text:
ImplicitDamageRatio extends explicit wind ratios with interior wind damage, utility wind damage, and flood damage. Use it when you need the component-level implicit ratios but do not need the final replacement-ratio-weighted building totals.

Related API: Damage Ratio Calculation API Related notebook: Fragility Curve Calculation with Detailed Damage Ratio Analysis

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
This class uses all ExplicitDamageRatio inputs plus loaded damage-ratio datasets:

  • ComponentCombination_All: shape (192, 6). The last column selects the one-based flood component configuration.
  • ProbDS_Flood: shape (8, 4, 136, 6), indexed by building type, flood configuration, flood depth, and damage state.
  • DamageState_Flood: shape (6, 2), used to sample flood damage values.
  • rng: optional seed or random generator for Weibull and flood sampling.

Indexing details:

  • ComponentConfigurationIndex is zero-based.
  • Flood configuration values inside ComponentCombination_All are one-based and validated before indexing ProbDS_Flood.
  • FloodDepthIndex is zero-based over the 136 flood-depth rows in the current probability file.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
With automatic execution:

  • ExplicitDamageRatioWind: inherited explicit wind dictionary.
  • ImplicitDamageRatioWind: dictionary with "Interior", "Electrical", "Mechanical", and "Plumbing".
  • tempProbDS_Flood: cumulative flood damage-state probabilities for the selected building type and component configuration, shape (136, 6).
  • ImplicitDamageRatioFlood: sampled scalar flood damage ratio.

Manual methods:

  • fn_damage_ratio_interior_wind() -> float
  • fn_damage_ratio_utility_wind() -> dict[str, float]
  • fn_helper_damage_ratio_flood() -> np.ndarray
  • fn_damage_ratio_flood() -> float

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, all flood and replacement-ratio datasets load in the base class. With it disabled, assign or load ProbDS_Flood, ComponentCombination_All, and DamageState_Flood before flood methods.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, explicit wind, implicit wind, flood helper, and flood damage calculations run during construction. With it disabled, call them in order: explicit wind first, interior wind, utility wind, flood helper, then flood damage.

docs.title: Automatic Example
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from types import SimpleNamespace
from cheersafe.damage_ratio_calculation import ImplicitDamageRatio
from cheersafe.inventory import BuildingInventory

building = BuildingInventory(buildings_file_name="BuildingGeometry.json").buildings[0]
resistance = {
    "Openings": np.ones(building.DoorFront + building.DoorBack + building.DoorGarage
                       + building.OpeningFront + building.OpeningBack
                       + 2 * (building.OpeningSideR + building.OpeningSideH)),
    "Walls": np.ones(12),
    "Roof Sheathings": np.ones(sum(building.NumPanel)),
    "Roof Coverings": np.ones(sum(building.NumPanel)),
    "Roof-Wall Connections": np.ones(sum(building.NumConnection)),
}
failure = SimpleNamespace(get_final_resistance=lambda: resistance)

implicit = ImplicitDamageRatio(building, failure, 0, 0, rng=1234)
print(implicit.ImplicitDamageRatioWind)
print(implicit.ImplicitDamageRatioFlood)

docs.title: Building
docs.text: cheersafe.inventory.Building represents one building archetype. It stores the 28 geometry and configuration values from a building-geometry input column and, when automatic execution is enabled, derives roof sheathing panel coordinates and roof-to-wall connection coordinates.

docs.title: Purpose And When To Use
docs.text: Use Building when you need to inspect or calculate geometry for one archetype, or when you are constructing an inventory manually. Most workflows receive Building instances from BuildingInventory instead of creating them one at a time.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Building takes 28 positional arguments. BuildingInventory passes each column of BuildingGeometry_Old.json or BuildingGeometry.json in this order.

Position Attribute Unit or code 1 BldgType 1-based building type ID. 2 Story Number of stories. 3 Material Material code. 4 WallFloorCon_FrontBack Count. 5 WallFloorCon_Side Count. 6 BldgLength ft. 7 BldgWidth ft. 8 MeanRoofHeight ft. 9 WallHeight ft. 10 OpeningFront Count. 11 OpeningBack Count. 12 OpeningSideR Count. 13 OpeningSideH Count. 14 OpeningLength ft. 15 OpeningWidth ft. 16 DoorFront Count. 17 DoorGarage Count. 18 DoorBack Count. 19 RoofShape 1 hip roof, 2 gable roof. 20 RoofPitchDegree degrees. 21 RoofPitch_r rise/run ratio. 22 RoofHeight ft. 23 RoofWidth ft. 24 HipRidgeLength ft. 25 HipRidgeAngle degrees. 26 TrussSpacing ft. 27 SheathingLength ft. 28 SheathingWidth ft.

The bundled geometry files have shape [28, 8]: rows are attributes, columns are building archetypes. The type annotations in Building coerce each constructor value to the expected Python type during __post_init__.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
When Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS is True, these attributes are assigned during initialization:

Attribute Shape or type Meaning PanelCoordinate Hip: [6, n]; gable: [4, n] Roof sheathing panel coordinates. Hip rows are left base x, right base x, left top x, right top x, base y, top y. Gable rows are left x, right x, base y, top y. Coordinates are in ft. NumPanel Hip: [4]; gable: [2] Panel counts by roof face. Hip order is front, back, side, side. Gable order is front, back. ConnectionCoordinate [n] Roof-to-wall connection coordinates in ft along the relevant roof edges. NumConnection Hip: length 4; gable: length 2 RWC counts by roof face, matching the roof-face order above.

fn_panel_coordinate() returns (panel_coordinate, num_panel). fn_connection_coordinate() returns (connection_coordinate, num_connection).

docs.title: AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS Behavior
docs.text: Building does not load files directly. This flag has no direct effect on a standalone Building. It matters when a BuildingInventory creates buildings from a JSON input file.

docs.title: AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, Building(...) computes and assigns PanelCoordinate, NumPanel, ConnectionCoordinate, and NumConnection.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = False, those attributes are not present after initialization. Call fn_panel_coordinate() and fn_connection_coordinate() manually and use their returned values.

from cheersafe.config import Config

print(building.BldgType)

docs.title: BuildingInventory
docs.text: cheersafe.inventory.BuildingInventory loads a building-geometry JSON file and creates one Building object per building-type column.

docs.title: Purpose And When To Use
docs.text: Use BuildingInventory for normal CHEERSafe workflows. Damage probability, damage ratio, and loss workflows expect an inventory object whose buildings attribute is a list of Building instances.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Default Unit, indexing, or file dependency buildings_file_name "BuildingGeometry_Old.json" File name under Config.INPUTS_PATH. The JSON must be a 2D list with shape [28, n_buildings]; rows follow the Building constructor order and columns are 1-based archetype IDs in the input data.

The default runtime path is Inputs/BuildingGeometry_Old.json. BuildingGeometry.json is the newer table with the same shape and schema, but the default loader still uses the old file unless you pass buildings_file_name="BuildingGeometry.json".

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
When the inventory is loaded, buildings is a list of Building objects. The bundled geometry files create 8 buildings.

instantiate_buildings_from_json() reads the JSON file, assigns self.buildings, and currently returns None.

docs.title: AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, BuildingInventory(...) immediately calls instantiate_buildings_from_json().

With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = False, initialization does not create buildings. Call instantiate_buildings_from_json() manually when you are ready to load the file.

docs.title: AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS Behavior
docs.text: BuildingInventory itself does not calculate geometry outputs. The flag is passed through indirectly because loading the inventory constructs Building objects. If AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, each loaded building has panel and RWC outputs. If it is False, the buildings are loaded but their calculation outputs must be requested manually from each building.

print(first.BldgType, first.PanelCoordinate.shape)

docs.title: Loads
docs.text:
The cheersafe.loads classes compute wind loads, component failures, and final resistance states for one building, one wind orientation, one wind speed, and one set of sampled component resistances.

Use these classes when you need the load/failure part of the CHEERSafe workflow without running the full damage-probability batch process. The usual end point is LoadingAndFailureCheck, which produces the final loads and final resistances consumed by damage-ratio calculations.

Related API: Loads API Planned notebook: loads workflow notebook

docs.title: Class Pages
docs.text:
• PreProcessLoad: pressure-zone coordinates and panel-zone area fractions.
  • InitialLoad: initial wind loads for roof, opening, wall, and roof-wall components.
  • InitialFailureCheck: first resistance update after initial loads.
  • FinalLoad: internal pressure and final loads after opening failure.
  • FinalFailureCheck: final component resistance update.
  • LoadingAndFailureCheck: public workflow wrapper for final loads and resistances.

docs.title: Shared Inputs
docs.text:
All load classes require:

  • Building: a cheersafe.inventory.Building with panel and roof-wall connection geometry already calculated. BuildingInventory creates these automatically when Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS and Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS are enabled.
  • WindOrientation: degrees, normally one of 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315.
  • WindSpeed: wind speed in mph for the wind-pressure equations.

Failure-check classes also require sampled or deterministic resistance arrays:

  • rRSt: roof sheathing resistance, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • rRCt: roof covering resistance, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • rRWCt: roof-wall connection resistance, shape (sum(Building.NumConnection),).
  • rOt: opening resistance, shape (DoorFront + DoorBack + DoorGarage + OpeningFront + OpeningBack + 2 * (OpeningSideR + OpeningSideH),).
  • rWt: wall resistance, shape (12,), flattened as four walls by three wall demand modes.

Load units follow the source implementation: wind speed is mph; pressure calculations use FPHLM/ASCE-style pressure coefficients and produce loads in the force units used by the resistance inputs.

docs.title: Dataset Loading
docs.text:
With Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, BaseLoad.__post_init__ loads these files from Config.INPUTS_PATH:

  • MWFRSCp.json, shape (8,)
  • CCRoofGCp.json, shape (3,)
  • CCWallGCp.json, shape (4,)

With Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = False, construct the class, assign MWFRSCp, CCRoofGCp, and CCWallGCp yourself, or call load_MWFRSCp(), load_CCRoofGCp(), and load_CCWallGCp() before executing methods that need them.

docs.title: Method Execution
docs.text:
With Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, constructors call the relevant fn_* methods and assign outputs to instance attributes.

With Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = False, constructors only set direct inputs and any unconditional setup. Call fn_* methods manually and assign the returned values you want to keep.

from cheersafe.inventory import BuildingInventory
from cheersafe.loads import InitialLoad

building = BuildingInventory(buildings_file_name="BuildingGeometry.json").buildings[0]
loads = InitialLoad(building, WindOrientation=0, WindSpeed=50)

print(loads.pRS.shape, loads.pW.shape)

from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.inventory import BuildingInventory
from cheersafe.loads import InitialLoad

building = BuildingInventory(buildings_file_name="BuildingGeometry.json").buildings[0]
old_execute = Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS
Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = False
try:
    loads = InitialLoad(building, WindOrientation=0, WindSpeed=50)
    loads.PressureZoneCoordinate, loads.NumZone = loads.fn_pressure_zone_coordinate()
    loads.PressureZoneArea, loads.PanelArea = loads.fn_preprocess_rs()
    loads.pRS = loads.fn_initial_load_rs()
finally:
    Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = old_execute

docs.title: FinalFailureCheck
docs.text:
FinalFailureCheck applies final loads to the current resistance state. It is the last calculation class before the public LoadingAndFailureCheck workflow wrapper.

Related API: Loads API Planned notebook: loads workflow notebook

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
The constructor takes the same arguments as FinalLoad: five resistance arrays, Building, WindOrientation, and WindSpeed.

The final check relies on these already-computed arrays when run manually:

  • pfRS, pfRC, pfRWC, pfO, pfW: final loads.
  • pInternal: scalar internal pressure.
  • rRSt, rRCt, rRWCt, rOt, rWt: current resistance arrays.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
With automatic execution:

  • rRSt: zeroed where pfRS > rRSt.
  • rRCt: zeroed where roof sheathing has failed or pfRC > rRCt.
  • rRWCt: updated roof-wall connection resistance.
  • rOt: zeroed where pfO > rOt.
  • rWt: zeroed where final wall loads exceed wall resistance.
  • RWCFails: shape (4,); side-level flags for roof-wall connection failure.

Manual return methods:

  • fn_final_failure_check_rwc() -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
  • fn_final_failure_check_w() -> np.ndarray

The class-level final resistance updates in __post_init__ are assignment behavior, not a separate return method.

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, coefficient files are loaded automatically. With it disabled, assign or load coefficients yourself.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, the full inherited chain runs and then final resistances are assigned. With it disabled, calculate the inherited outputs first, then call the two final-check helper methods and apply the same assignment logic needed by your workflow.

docs.title: Automatic Example
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from cheersafe.inventory import BuildingInventory
from cheersafe.loads import FinalFailureCheck
from cheersafe.tools import Utils

building = BuildingInventory(buildings_file_name="BuildingGeometry.json").buildings[0]
mean = Utils.from_json("Inputs/MeanResistanceValue.json")

check = FinalFailureCheck(
    np.full(sum(building.NumPanel), mean[1, 0]),
    np.full(sum(building.NumPanel), mean[0, 0]),
    np.full(sum(building.NumConnection), mean[2, 0]),
    np.full(building.DoorFront + building.DoorBack + building.DoorGarage
            + building.OpeningFront + building.OpeningBack
            + 2 * (building.OpeningSideR + building.OpeningSideH), mean[3, 0]),
    np.full(12, mean[4, 0]),
    building,
    0,
    50,
)
print(check.RWCFails)

docs.title: FinalLoad
docs.text:
FinalLoad calculates internal pressure after the initial failure check and then computes final component loads. Use it when opening failures may change internal pressure and therefore roof, wall, and opening demands.

Related API: Loads API Planned notebook: loads workflow notebook

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
FinalLoad inherits all inputs from InitialFailureCheck: building, wind orientation, wind speed, coefficient datasets, and five resistance arrays.

Important shape expectations:

  • roof sheathing and roof covering arrays: (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • roof-wall connection arrays: (sum(Building.NumConnection),).
  • opening arrays: total door/window count.
  • wall arrays: (12,) for resistances and (4, 3) for wall loads.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
With automatic execution:

  • pInternal: scalar internal pressure after initial opening failure.
  • pfRS: final roof sheathing load, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • pfRC: final roof covering load, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • pfRWC: final roof-wall connection load, shape (sum(Building.NumConnection),).
  • pfO: final opening load, usually array-like with total opening count.
  • pfW: final wall load matrix, shape (4, 3).

Manual methods return these outputs: fn_pressure_internal(), fn_final_load_rs(), fn_final_load_rc(), fn_final_load_rwc(), fn_final_load_o(), and fn_final_load_w().

If pInternal == 0, the constructor reuses initial loads for pfRS, pfRWC, pfO, and pfW instead of recalculating them.

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, coefficient files are loaded automatically. With it disabled, assign or load coefficients before running load methods.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, preprocessing, initial loads, initial failure checks, internal pressure, and final loads run during construction. With it disabled, follow that same order manually. fn_final_load_w() reads pInternal, so assign it first.

docs.title: InitialFailureCheck
docs.text:
InitialFailureCheck compares initial loads with component resistance arrays and returns the first updated resistance state. Use it when you need the opening, wall, and roof sheathing failures that drive internal-pressure recalculation.

Related API: Loads API Planned notebook: loads workflow notebook

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
This class has all InitialLoad inputs plus resistance arrays:

  • rRSt: roof sheathing resistance, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • rRCt: roof covering resistance, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • rRWCt: roof-wall connection resistance, shape (sum(Building.NumConnection),).
  • rOt: opening resistance, shape equal to total doors plus windows.
  • rWt: wall resistance, shape (12,).

The example below uses Inputs/MeanResistanceValue.json as a deterministic resistance source. Production simulations usually pass sampled values.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
With automatic execution, the instance updates:

  • rRSt: entries become 0 where pRS > rRSt.
  • rRCt: copied unchanged by the initial check.
  • rRWCt: copied unchanged by the initial check.
  • rOt: entries become 0 where pO >= rOt.
  • rWt: entries become 0 where flattened wall loads exceed wall resistance.

fn_initial_failure_check() returns a dictionary keyed by "Roof Sheathings", "Roof Coverings", "Roof-Wall Connections", "Openings", and "Walls". It does not mutate the original arrays unless the caller assigns the returned values.

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, load coefficient files are read automatically. With it disabled, provide the coefficient arrays before load methods run.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, initial loads and the initial failure check run during construction. With it disabled, calculate and assign pRS, pO, and pW before calling fn_initial_failure_check().

docs.title: InitialLoad
docs.text:
InitialLoad calculates the first-pass wind loads on roof sheathings, roof coverings, roof-wall connections, openings, and walls. Use it after preprocessing when you need component demands before any failure state changes internal pressure.

Related API: Loads API Planned notebook: loads workflow notebook

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Building: cheersafe.inventory.Building with PanelCoordinate, NumPanel, ConnectionCoordinate, and NumConnection.
  • WindOrientation: degrees, normally one of the eight directions in Inputs/WindOrientation.json.
  • WindSpeed: mph for the wind-pressure equations.
  • Loaded coefficient datasets: MWFRSCp, CCRoofGCp, and CCWallGCp.
  • Preprocessing outputs: PressureZoneCoordinate, NumZone, PressureZoneArea, and PanelArea.

The class computes qh = 0.00256 * 0.85 * WindSpeed ** 2 during construction regardless of AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
With automatic execution:

  • pRS: initial roof sheathing load, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).
  • pRC: initial roof covering load, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),). The current implementation returns the same array as pRS.
  • pRWC: initial roof-wall connection load, shape (sum(Building.NumConnection),).
  • pO: opening load, length equal to the total door/window opening count.
  • pW: wall load matrix, shape (4, 3).

Manual methods return one output each: fn_initial_load_rs(), fn_initial_load_rc(), fn_initial_load_rwc(), fn_initial_load_o(), and fn_initial_load_w().

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, coefficient JSON files load from Inputs/. With it disabled, assign or load the coefficient arrays before calling the fn_initial_load_* methods.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, preprocessing and all initial loads are calculated during construction. With it disabled, call preprocessing first, then call the initial-load methods. fn_initial_load_w() depends on pRWC, so calculate or assign pRWC before wall loads.

print(loads.qh)
print(loads.pRS.shape, loads.pRWC.shape, loads.pW.shape)

docs.title: LoadingAndFailureCheck
docs.text:
LoadingAndFailureCheck is the public load workflow class. It inherits the full FinalFailureCheck chain and adds convenience getters for final loads and final resistances.

Use this class when you want the output object passed into cheersafe.damage_ratio_calculation.DamageRatioCalculation.

Related API: Loads API Planned notebook: loads workflow notebook

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Constructor inputs:

  • rRSt, rRCt, rRWCt, rOt, rWt: resistance arrays with the shapes described in the loads overview.
  • Building: cheersafe.inventory.Building.
  • WindOrientation: degrees.
  • WindSpeed: mph for the wind-pressure equations.

update_inputs_and_outputs() accepts the same inputs and reruns the workflow by calling update_outputs().

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
Inherited automatic attributes include all initial loads, final loads, final resistances, pInternal, and RWCFails.

Public getters:

  • get_final_resistance() -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
  • get_final_loads() -> dict[str, np.ndarray]

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, coefficient files are loaded automatically. With it disabled, assign or load coefficients before execution.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, the complete workflow runs during construction. With it disabled, get_final_resistance() and get_final_loads() only work after you have manually populated the corresponding attributes.

docs.title: PreProcessLoad
docs.text:
PreProcessLoad prepares roof pressure-zone geometry before any component loads are calculated. Use it when you need to inspect pressure-zone coordinates, panel areas, or the fraction of each roof panel inside ASCE pressure zones.

Related API: Loads API Planned notebook: loads workflow notebook

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Building: cheersafe.inventory.Building. Required geometry includes RoofShape, HipRidgeAngle, BldgLength, BldgWidth, RoofWidth, MeanRoofHeight, SheathingLength, SheathingWidth, PanelCoordinate, and NumPanel.
  • WindOrientation: degrees. Pressure-zone layout changes with orientation.
  • WindSpeed: mph for the wind-pressure equations. Accepted by the base load class, but preprocessing geometry does not use the speed directly.
  • Optional defaults: G=0.85, GCpi=0.18; these are inherited but not central to preprocessing.

Required files when Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True: Inputs/MWFRSCp.json, Inputs/CCRoofGCp.json, and Inputs/CCWallGCp.json.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
When automatic execution is enabled, the instance receives:

  • PressureZoneCoordinate: pressure-zone coordinate tensor. For the first sample building this is shape (8, 4, 4).
  • NumZone: list of zone counts by roof side. For the first sample building at 0 degrees this is [4, 1, 1, 1].
  • PressureZoneArea: panel area fractions by pressure zone, shape (3, sum(Building.NumPanel)).
  • PanelArea: panel areas, shape (sum(Building.NumPanel),).

Manual methods return the same values:

  • fn_pressure_zone_coordinate() -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[int]]
  • fn_preprocess_rs() -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

docs.title: Config Behavior
docs.text:
With AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS = True, pressure coefficient files load during construction. With it disabled, load or assign MWFRSCp, CCRoofGCp, and CCWallGCp before later load calculations need them.

With AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS = True, PressureZoneCoordinate, NumZone, PressureZoneArea, and PanelArea are populated during construction. With it disabled, call fn_pressure_zone_coordinate() before fn_preprocess_rs(), because preprocessing reads PressureZoneCoordinate and NumZone.

pre = PreProcessLoad(building, WindOrientation=0, WindSpeed=50)

print(pre.PressureZoneArea.shape)
print(pre.PanelArea.sum())

docs.title: Loss Estimation
docs.text: Use this module after damage probabilities are available to estimate monetary losses at building, component, and regional scales. Loss estimation combines hurricane hazard data, building values, inventory counts, and damage-state probability surfaces.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Page Use when DamageProbabilityProvider You need damage ratios for specific hazard intensities and (m, c) combinations. BuildingLossEstimator You need building-by-hurricane losses from building values and hazard arrays. ComponentLossEstimator You need losses aggregated to zone, building type, component configuration, and hurricane. RegionalLossEstimator You need total regional loss per hurricane. LossEstimation You want the end-to-end orchestrator for building, component, regional, and loss-ratio outputs.

docs.title: Shared Inputs
docs.text: File Shape Units or indexing Used by Inputs/Hurricane_ProbWindFlood.json object Arrays keyed by hurricane probability, wind speed, flood depth, and flood ratio. All loss estimators. Inputs/DamageState.json [50, 2] damage-state id, damage ratio Base estimators and provider. Inputs/WindSpeed.json [25, 3] id, mph, m/s Provider bin lookup uses column 2. Inputs/FloodDepth.json [136, 3] id, inches, meters Provider bin lookup uses column 2. Outputs/ProbDS_wfd_dictMaxIter{NUM_OF_ITERATIONS}_aggregated.pkl dict[(m, c), array] Building type and 1-based component configuration keys. Damage provider. Inputs/Building_imc_Component_ZTRAXPropValueSample.csv rows x 13 Building records with ind_1509, m, c, and value columns. Building losses. Inputs/X_imc.json [1509, 8, 192] Zone, building type, component configuration counts. Regional losses.

docs.title: Configuration Behavior
docs.text:
Important current nuance: BaseLossEstimator and DamageProbabilityProvider load their datasets in __post_init__ without checking Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS. Setting AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS=False does not stop their constructors from loading files today.

The loss-estimation classes also do not use Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS to run loss calculations. Constructing an estimator loads inputs and nested helper objects; call calculate_* or estimate_* methods explicitly to produce loss arrays and output files.

from cheersafe.loss_estimation import DamageProbabilityProvider

docs.title: BuildingLossEstimator
docs.text: BuildingLossEstimator calculates building-level loss for each hurricane event. Use it when you need a building-by-hurricane loss matrix and the building-value CSV is the working exposure sample.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Inherited file inputs:

Input Default Notes hurricane_data_path Inputs/Hurricane_ProbWindFlood.json Contains Hurricane_Prob, Hurricane_WindSpeed, Hurricane_FloodDepth, and Hurricane_FloodRatio. damage_state_path Inputs/DamageState.json Loaded by the base estimator. wind_speed_path Inputs/WindSpeed.json Hazard bin table. flood_depth_path Inputs/FloodDepth.json Hazard bin table. peril HURR One of WIND, FLOOD, or HURR.

Input Default Shape or columns building_values_path Inputs/Building_imc_Component_ZTRAXPropValueSample.csv Must include ind_1509, m, c, and improvement_value. damage_provider None When None, a new DamageProbabilityProvider is created.
