docs.title: LossEstimation
docs.text: LossEstimation is the end-to-end orchestrator for loss workflows. Use it when you want one object to coordinate damage-probability lookup, wind and flood building losses, component losses, regional losses, and loss-ratio outputs.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Required constructor inputs:

Input Type Notes hurricane_data_path str Path to hurricane probability, wind, flood, and flood-ratio data. inventory_path str Path to X_imc inventory counts.

Optional inputs:

Input Default Notes building_values_path Inputs/Building_imc_Component_ZTRAXPropValueSample.csv Building-level values and component configuration sample. prob_ds_file_path None Passed to DamageProbabilityProvider; default uses Config.OUTPUTS_PATH and Config.NUM_OF_ITERATIONS. output_dir Outputs Created during initialization.

During initialization the class creates one shared DamageProbabilityProvider, wind and flood building estimators, wind and flood component estimators, and a regional estimator.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
Method Returns Files estimate_building_losses(peril) Dict with peril, building_losses, and output_path. Outputs/L_bh_{peril}.json; for direct building estimators, CSV tables are also written. estimate_component_losses(peril) Dict with peril, component_losses, and output_path. Outputs/L_imch_Single_{peril}.json. estimate_regional_losses(peril) Dict with peril, regional_losses, and output_path. Outputs/HurricaneLoss_{peril}.json. estimate_all_losses() Dict containing building, component, regional, and loss-ratio results. All files above plus loss-ratio JSON files.

peril is one of WIND, FLOOD, or HURR.

docs.title: RegionalLossEstimator
docs.text: RegionalLossEstimator combines component losses with the regional inventory to estimate total loss per hurricane. Use it when the desired output is a regional hurricane-loss vector rather than building-level or component-level arrays.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Inherited base inputs are loaded from the hurricane, damage-state, wind-speed, and flood-depth files.

Class-specific inputs:

Input Default Shape or notes inventory_path Inputs/X_imc.json Inventory counts shaped [i, 8, 192]. component_loss_estimator None When None, a new component estimator is created. peril HURR WIND, FLOOD, or HURR.

For FLOOD, the hurricane flood-ratio array is broadcast over building type and component configuration. For HURR, the current implementation computes separate wind and flood regional losses and adds them.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
Method Returns Files calculate_regional_losses() hurricane_losses shaped [h]. Outputs/HurricaneLoss_{peril}.json. combine_wind_flood_losses() Combined hurricane losses shaped [h]. Outputs/HurricaneLoss_HURR.json.

Returned arrays are not automatically assigned to self.hurricane_losses inside these calculation methods.

docs.title: Configuration Behavior
docs.text: Construction loads base datasets and inventory regardless of Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS. Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS does not run regional calculations automatically.

docs.title: Minimal Examples
docs.text:
Automatic initialization:

from cheersafe.loss_estimation import RegionalLossEstimator

estimator = RegionalLossEstimator(peril="WIND")
wind, flood = estimator.get_adjusted_hazard_data()

Manual dependency control:

from cheersafe.loss_estimation import ComponentLossEstimator, RegionalLossEstimator

component_estimator = ComponentLossEstimator(peril="FLOOD")
regional_estimator = RegionalLossEstimator(
    component_loss_estimator=component_estimator,
    peril="FLOOD",
)
# For a full run:
# losses = regional_estimator.calculate_regional_losses()
# regional_estimator.hurricane_losses["FLOOD"] = losses

docs.title: Covariance
docs.text: cheersafe.tools.Covariance builds covariance matrices from component counts, mean values, coefficients of variation, and correlation assumptions.

docs.title: Purpose And When To Use
docs.text: Use Covariance.create_cov_matrix() before Latin hypercube sampling when component samples should share intra-component and inter-component correlation. Damage probability workflows use this pattern for correlated component resistance sampling.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Unit, indexing, or shape num_component List of component group sizes. The sum is the matrix dimension. temp_mean NumPy array of mean values, one per element after expanding all groups. Units match the sampled quantity, such as psf or lbs. Shape [sum(num_component)]. temp_cv NumPy array of coefficients of variation, same shape as temp_mean. Unitless. inter_correlation Correlation between elements in different component groups. Default 0.2. intra_correlation Correlation between elements in the same component group. Default 0.4.

Inputs are zero-indexed Python arrays/lists. The group order in num_component defines the block structure of the returned matrix.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text:
create_cov_matrix() returns a NumPy array with shape [sum(num_component), sum(num_component)]. Diagonal values are (temp_mean * temp_cv) ** 2. Off-diagonal values are the selected correlation coefficient multiplied by the outer product of standard deviations.

No files are read or written, and no class or instance state is assigned.

docs.title: AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS Behavior
docs.text: Covariance does not load files and does not inspect Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS.

docs.title: AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS Behavior
docs.text: Covariance has no constructor and no automatic execution behavior. The matrix is created only when create_cov_matrix() is called.

docs.title: Minimal Automatic Example
docs.text:
There is no constructor-side automatic behavior for Covariance; the direct call is the normal use:

PYTHONPATH=src python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
from cheersafe.tools import Covariance

sigma = Covariance.create_cov_matrix(
    [2, 1],
    np.array([10.0, 12.0, 8.0]),
    np.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.15]),
)
print(sigma.shape)
print(np.round(np.diag(sigma), 3).tolist())
PY

docs.title: Minimal Manual-Control Example
docs.text:
PYTHONPATH=src python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
from cheersafe.tools import Covariance, Sampling

mean = np.array([10.0, 12.0, 8.0])
cv = np.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.15])
sigma = Covariance.create_cov_matrix(
    [2, 1],
    mean,
    cv,
    inter_correlation=0.1,
    intra_correlation=0.5,
)
samples = Sampling.generate_lhs_samples_norm(5, mean, sigma, seed=11)

print(sigma.shape)
print(samples.shape)
PY

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text: cheersafe.tools.Sampling provides deterministic random-number helpers and Latin hypercube sampling methods.

docs.title: Purpose And When To Use
docs.text: Use Sampling when you need CHEERSafe's centralized seed policy or want to generate component samples with normal or SciPy-supported marginal distributions. Damage probability workflows use these helpers to make stochastic simulation reproducible.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Method Inputs Units, indexing, or shapes resolve_seed(seed=None) Optional seed. Returns Config.RANDOM_SEED when seed is None; otherwise returns int(seed). derive_seed(label, *parts, seed=None) Text label, seed parts, optional base seed. Produces a deterministic 32-bit seed from JSON-stable normalized inputs. create_rng(seed=None) Optional seed, NumPy Generator, or RNG-like object. Returns a fresh NumPy generator for numeric seeds; returns supplied generator/RNG-like objects. random(rng=None) Optional seed or RNG. Returns one uniform random value in [0, 1). permutation(n, rng=None) Integer n, optional seed or RNG. Returns a permutation of np.arange(n). weibull_min(shape, scale, rng=None) Weibull shape and scale. Returns one zero-location Weibull-min draw multiplied by scale. generate_lhs_samples_norm(n, mean, covariance, seed=None) Sample count, mean vector, covariance matrix, optional seed. mean length is the dimension d; covariance shape is [d, d]; return shape is [n, d]. generate_lhs_samples_general(n, distributions_details, mean, covariance, seed=None) Sample count, SciPy distribution specs, means, covariance, optional seed. distributions_details length must be 1 or d. Each dict needs a SciPy distribution type, such as "norm" or "lognorm". Return shape is [n, d].

generate_lhs_samples_* pass Config.NUM_OF_WORKERS_SAMPLING to SciPy's LatinHypercube random() call.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text: All Sampling methods return values directly and do not assign state. generate_lhs_samples_norm() and generate_lhs_samples_general() return NumPy arrays with rows as samples and columns as variables.

docs.title: AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS Behavior
docs.text: Sampling does not load files and does not inspect Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS.

docs.title: AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS Behavior
docs.text: Sampling has no constructor and no automatic execution behavior. The methods run only when called.

docs.title: Minimal Automatic Example
docs.text:
There is no constructor-side automatic behavior for Sampling; the direct call is the normal use:

PYTHONPATH=src python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.tools import Sampling

Config.reset_flags()
samples = Sampling.generate_lhs_samples_norm(
    4,
    np.array([10.0, 20.0]),
    np.array([[1.0, 0.2], [0.2, 4.0]]),
    seed=7,
)
print(samples.shape)
print(np.round(samples.mean(axis=0), 2))

Config.reset_flags()
PY

docs.title: Minimal Manual-Control Example
docs.text:
PYTHONPATH=src python3 - <<'PY'
from cheersafe.config import Config
from cheersafe.tools import Sampling

Config.reset_flags()
Config.RANDOM_SEED = 123

seed = Sampling.derive_seed("component", 1, {"config": 2})
rng = Sampling.create_rng(seed)

print(seed)
print(round(Sampling.random(rng), 6))
print(Sampling.permutation(5, rng).tolist())

Config.reset_flags()
PY

docs.title: Utils
docs.text: cheersafe.tools.Utils contains lightweight file and DataFrame helpers used by the CHEERSafe runtime.

docs.title: Purpose And When To Use
docs.text: Use Utils.from_json() and Utils.to_json() for the same JSON conversion rules used by the model. Use Utils.filter_column_values_df() when you need the first matching value from a pandas table after applying simple equality filters.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Method Inputs Units, indexing, shapes, or file dependencies from_json(path_to_file, dict_key=None) JSON file path and optional dictionary key. JSON lists are converted to NumPy arrays. JSON dictionaries return the full dictionary unless dict_key is supplied, in which case that value is converted to a NumPy array. to_json(data, path_to_file) JSON-compatible data, NumPy arrays/scalars, nested lists, tuples, or dictionaries. Parent directories are created when needed. NumPy arrays become lists and NumPy scalars become Python scalars. filter_column_values_df(df, column_name, **kwargs) pandas DataFrame, output column name, and equality filters by column. Filters are exact equality conditions. The method returns the first matching row's selected column value as a NumPy array.

Utils does not use Config.INPUTS_PATH automatically. Pass the full path you want to read or write.

docs.title: Outputs And Returns
docs.text: Method Return from_json() np.ndarray for JSON lists or selected dictionary values; dict for full JSON objects. to_json() None; writes a JSON file. filter_column_values_df() np.ndarray containing the selected value from the first matching row.

docs.title: AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS Behavior
docs.text: Utils methods do not inspect Config.AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS. They perform their I/O or filtering only when called.

docs.title: AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS Behavior
docs.text: Utils methods do not inspect Config.AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS. They are class methods with no automatic initialization behavior.

docs.title: Minimal Automatic Example
docs.text:
There is no constructor-side automatic behavior for Utils; the direct call is the normal use:

PYTHONPATH=src python3 - <<'PY'
from cheersafe.tools import Utils

geometry = Utils.from_json("Inputs/BuildingGeometry_Old.json")
print(geometry.shape)
print(geometry[:, 0].shape)
PY

docs.title: Minimal Manual-Control Example
docs.text:
PYTHONPATH=src python3 - <<'PY'
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import pandas as pd
from cheersafe.tools import Utils

df = pd.DataFrame({"BldgType": [1, 2], "Value": [[10, 20], [30, 40]]})
value = Utils.filter_column_values_df(df, "Value", BldgType=2)

with TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    out = f"{tmpdir}/manual_utils_example.json"
    Utils.to_json({"value": value}, out)
    print(Utils.from_json(out))
PY
